notable_absence.finding: The page opens with a raw, unresolved porting marker directly in the rendered body text: '**TODO: Scala -→ Python**' - immediately followed by a paragraph and code sample that ARE in Python (UpsertOptions/ServerDurability), suggesting the page was copied from the Scala SDK's equivalent concept page and partially, but not completely, adapted; the TODO marker itself was never cleaned up before publishing. This is the same authorship-provenance class of issue flagged in round 29's CLI stress test, now found in the Python SDK's own docs tree - worth surfacing to the reconciler/docs-issues process even though this batch does not write to docs-issues directly.

cross_component_finding: The entire 'Preferred Server Group Replica Reads' section (heading, prose, and CAUTION box) is duplicated verbatim between this page and howtos/kv-operations.md in the same batch - both extraction records file it under the same minted id, sdk:preferred-server-group-replica-reads, since it is genuinely one piece of content appearing on two pages rather than two independent descriptions.
cross_product_finding: This page is Python's closest analogue to whatever concept page anchors Java SDK round 4's sdk:transaction-durability/sdk:transaction-attempt-context findings, but its own leftover '**TODO: Scala -> Python**' marker is itself a strong signal that this specific page's prose should NOT be trusted as an authoritative, Python-native description - it may be describing Scala idioms that were only partially translated. Where this page's durability-levels bullet list is concerned, the content is identical to howtos/kv-operations.md's (same three ServerDurability levels, same wording), so reuse of sdk:durability/durability:level-majority/etc. here is safe despite the provenance flag. But sdk:pessimistic-locking and sdk:replica-reads are minted fresh from this page's prose with that caveat attached - if a future Scala-SDK extraction round turns up the same 'get-and-lock'/'unlock' language, that would be strong evidence this page's content did originate from Scala's docs and both should point to one shared underlying id rather than being SDK-independent mints.
